sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK technique impact model (LBRO curated)

T1110.rationale: Successful brute force primarily compromises authentication secrets; further data access requires follow-on actions.

T1046.rationale: Port scanning alone does not demonstrate access to personal data stores.

T1499.rationale: Endpoint DoS affects availability; does not by itself imply confidentiality breach.

T1498.rationale: Network DoS affects availability without demonstrating data exfiltration.

T1071.rationale: C2 channels may carry commands or stolen data; flow metadata cannot confirm content.

T1189.rationale: Drive-by style web attacks may lead to client-side compromise affecting users visiting the service.

T1190.rationale: Exploitation of a public application may expose backend databases tied to that application.

T1021.rationale: Remote service access may reach systems holding business or personal data.

T1048.rationale: Exfiltration techniques imply data leaving the environment; treat linked asset categories as at risk when exfiltration is confirmed by class mapping.
